TreVeyon Henderson.note: Ruled out for the season opener after missing all game-week practices with the ankle injury suffered Aug. 24. Week 2 remains uncertain.

Zach Charbonnet.note: Unavailable for at least the first four games while rehabbing a torn ACL. Seattle has been encouraged by his rehab, but there is no firm return date.

Tory Horton.note: Was limited throughout game week and inactive for Seattle's opener. Hamstring issue follows an injury-interrupted 2025 season.

George Kittle.note: No final game designation and expected to play, but San Francisco has indicated it will manage his workload in his return from the Achilles tear.

Rome Odunze.note: Limited on the first Week 1 report with a new calf injury after sitting out earlier work. Day-to-day and not yet fully cleared.

Jonathon Brooks.note: Returned to team practice as a limited participant while working back from a second ACL tear and current groin soreness. Even if active, an early-season workload cap is likely.

Zay Flowers.note: Limited on Baltimore's first Week 1 injury report with a hamstring issue but currently expects to play Sunday.

Michael Penix Jr..note: Practiced fully, but Atlanta has confirmed Penix will be inactive for Week 1 while the team continues a cautious return-to-game ramp following his 2025 ACL tear. The full practice is encouraging, but game availability has not yet been restored.
Michael Penix Jr..expectedReturn: Week 2 or later; no firm game-return date

Tua Tagovailoa.note: Developed back discomfort during Thursday practice and was limited, with Cooper Rush taking first-team reps afterward. Tua had been named Atlanta's Week 1 starter, but his availability for Sunday is now in question.

Alvin Kamara.note: Returned to practice as a limited participant after an MCL sprain. Availability has improved, but Week 1 workload remains uncertain.

Isiah Pacheco.note: On injured reserve and must miss at least four games. Detroit has not provided a firm return timetable.

Tank Dell.note: On injured reserve with a knee issue and unavailable until at least Week 5.

James Conner.note: On injured reserve with a foot injury and unavailable for the opening portion of the season.

Jeremiyah Love.note: Arizona is optimistic he can play Week 1, but he is returning from a high-ankle sprain and is listed behind Tyler Allgeier on the unofficial depth chart. Initial workload could be reduced.

Josh Jacobs.note: Currently unavailable to play because of an off-field league status with no established football return date. This adjustment reflects availability uncertainty, not injury performance risk.

Brock Bowers.note: Underwent a meniscus trim and is expected to miss one to two games. No major long-term efficiency penalty is assumed yet.

Malik Nabers.note: Full participant and expected to play Week 1. A small workload and post-ACL risk modifier remains until normal game usage is confirmed.

Xavier Legette.note: Not listed on Carolina's Week 1 injury report after recovering from the August ankle injury and walking-boot period. He is medically cleared for the opener; any playing-time limitation is role-based rather than injury-based.

Jakobi Meyers.note: Practicing in a non-contact jersey with a thumb injury. Current concern is primarily Week 1 workload rather than long-term availability.

Marvin Mims Jr..note: Was not spotted at Monday practice while managing a foot issue. Week 1 participation still needs confirmation.

Patrick Mahomes.note: Fully cleared following ACL/LCL rehabilitation and expected to start Week 1. Mahomes has reported no planned playing restrictions; only a minimal residual long-term post-reconstruction risk modifier remains until regular-season game action is confirmed.

A.J. Brown.note: Exited New England's Week 1 game with a right ankle injury and did not return. X-rays reportedly showed no fracture, but a high-ankle sprain is suspected and MRI results are pending. Initial adjustment is intentionally conservative until the absence timeline is confirmed.
A.J. Brown.expectedReturn: TBD after MRI; multi-week absence possible

Sam Darnold.status: OUT Week 2 - hip strain; no structural damage
Sam Darnold.note: Follow-up testing showed no structural damage after the right hip injury suffered in Seattle's opener. The injury is muscular rather than a fracture or major structural issue. Darnold is expected to miss Week 2, with a possible return in Week 3 if his recovery progresses normally.

Alec Pierce.note: Practiced on a limited basis on Indianapolis' first Week 1 injury report while returning from heel surgery. He is trending toward availability, so the adjustment is limited primarily to possible early workload restriction.
